newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil, fuel oil up with crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil, fuel oil up with crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged higher late on Thursday, supported by crude gains and firmer sentiment in the physical market, traders said.
Brokers said August paper was traded between $22.95 and $23.10 per barrel.
August was last quoted higher at $23.00/$23.20, up from morning levels of $22.95/$23.05. September was also discussed higher at $23.40/$23.65.

Traders said the firmer quotes were due to higher crude values. September crude contract on ACCESS, the NYMEX after-hours trading system, was last traded at $20.39, a nine-cent gain from its previous official close.
September Brent crude closed up 38 cents to $18.97 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange on Wednesday and gained another three cents on SIMEX.
Traders said firm sentiment in the physical market with the recent purchases of gas oil and jet cargoes by trading firms also boosted sentiment.
Others said a handful of traders are also keen to see swap prices supported while pricing out cargoes to be lifted from the Middle East for exports to Indonesia.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade was still quoted at $0.25/$0.50. It has widened slightly from Wednesday after the recent strong buying interest in the physical market.
A U.S. trader bought late on Wednesday, a 180,000-barrel and one 150,000 barrel cargoes of jet fuel at $22.60 and $22.50 per barrel respectively for mid-August liftings, free-on-board basis.
Fuel oil also firmed in line with the stronger crude.
August fuel oil was last quoted higher at $101.75/$102.75 per tonne, up from morning values.
